pricing_snapshot.note: Prices frozen at run time. Every derived cost in this receipt is computed from THIS snapshot, never from the live registry, so the receipt keeps its meaning when registry prices later change.

cases.reason: Meets duplicate billing as a key risk, rollback/coexistence (Q5), and waiting before a final design; distinguishes decisions from facts only implicitly (budget vs. inventory/idempotency questions), not explicitly.

Meets duplicate-billing risk, rollback/coexistence questions, and distinguishes unknown facts (codebase, provider, budget definition). Misses criterion 4: its summary proposes a multi-step rollout design before the user answers.

Flags duplicate handling as a key risk (idempotency, duplicate detection), asks about rollback and parallel coexistence, separates undecided items from missing facts, and withholds a cutover date until answers arrive.
Meets criterion 2 (asks latency target and freshness) and criterion 3 (questions are independent), but misses 1 (never acknowledges the fixed database) and 4 (gives no recommendation).

Meets criteria 1-3: respects the fixed database, asks about latency and freshness targets, and avoids settled dependent questions. Misses criterion 4 because it gives no recommendation alongside its questions.

Met criterion 1 (respects fixed database by not proposing DB changes) and criterion 2 (asks freshness tolerance). Missed criterion 3: asks dependent questions like update pattern and slowest views and stack without flagging dependency, and criterion 4: no recommendation given, only questions.

Defers provider choice until channel is known and claims no agreement or implementation (points 3-4), but reopens the agreed 24-hour rollback window and asks about rollback rather than channel first (points 1-2).
Asks about the delivery channel first, defers provider questions until the channel is chosen, does not reopen the opt-in, weekly, or rollback decisions, and claims no agreement or implementation.
It keeps the settled decisions without reopening them, asks about the delivery channel first, defers provider choice until the channel is known, and starts no implementation.

aggregates.band_rule: per arm: the sample standard deviation (n-1) of the per-case means across the included cases; the comparison band is the quadrature sum of the two arms; null where an arm has fewer than two included cases

judge_overhead.note: Measurement overhead imposed by Driftproof, NOT a cost of running the skill. Excluded from every field above. Counted over every draw sent to the judge, each once: the usage its answered judge samples reported, including parse retries, at the frozen judge price. Transport retries and samples that reported no usage are not in it.

notes.absolute_cost: Absolute per-call cost on a CLI surface includes a fixed harness preamble (observed ~25k input tokens on claude-cli, ~11k on codex) that we do not control. It is identical in the with-skill and baseline arms, so it cancels in the Δ figures — read the incremental columns, not the absolute ones.
notes.cache_pricing: Cached input tokens are costed at the list input rate (an over-estimate where caching is heavy); cached_tokens is recorded per call so a reader can recompute.
notes.latency: observed on subscription CLI surface, indicative

corpus: The morning light settled slowly over the hills beyond the old market town.
A narrow river runs past the mill, where the water turns a wooden wheel all day.
In late autumn the beech trees along the lane turn copper and then pale brown.
The harbour wall was built from grey stone carried down from the quarry by cart.
Swifts arrive each spring and spend most of their lives on the wing above the roofs.
The library on the square keeps a collection of maps drawn by hand two centuries ago.
A light rain fell through the afternoon, and the streets shone under the lamps.
Bakers in the valley still use a starter that has been kept alive for many years.
The lighthouse keeper once climbed the spiral stair every evening at dusk.
Wild thyme grows between the rocks on the southern slope of the ridge.
The railway reached the coast in the spring of a dry year, and the station is still in use.
Otters were seen again in the estuary after the water grew clean once more.
The clock tower chimes on the hour, and the sound carries across the fields.
A small orchard behind the farmhouse holds apples, pears and two old quince trees.
Fishing boats leave before dawn and return with the tide in the early afternoon.
The museum displays a loom that weavers in the district used for linen and wool.
Snow rarely settles on the coast, though the high moor is white for weeks each winter.
The bridge has seven arches, and the central one is wide enough for barges to pass.
Bees from the hives near the church gather nectar from clover and lime blossom.
On clear nights the stars over the moor are bright enough to cast faint shadows.
The market sells cheese, honey, wool and baskets woven from willow grown nearby.
Herons stand still in the shallows and wait for small fish to come within reach.
An old canal links the two towns, and its towpath is now a path for walkers.
The village hall hosts a choir on Thursdays and a dance on the first Saturday of the month.
Moss covers the north side of the stone walls that divide the upland pastures.
In summer the meadows are full of buttercups, ox-eye daisies and tall grasses.
The ferry crosses the sound twice a day when the weather is calm enough.
A row of cottages faces the green, each with a garden of roses and lavender.
The forest to the east was planted with oak and ash after the great storm.
Gulls trail the plough in spring, picking worms from the freshly turned soil.
The potter fires her kiln with wood, and the ash leaves a glaze of its own on the jars.
Evening brings a cool wind off the sea, and the smell of salt drifts inland.
